title: Tech & The Web
subject: Computing and the internet
blurb: Acronyms, origin stories and the names things had before they had good names.

questions.prompt: Who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web?
questions.hint: He wrote the proposal at CERN in 1989, and his boss called it 'vague but exciting'.
questions.note: Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn built the internet's plumbing - TCP/IP. The Web sits on top of it.

questions.prompt: Which programming language was created by Guido van Rossum?
questions.hint: Named after a comedy troupe, not the snake.

questions.prompt: What does the S in HTTPS stand for?
questions.hint: It is what the padlock in the address bar is promising you.

questions.prompt: Which search engine was originally called BackRub?
questions.hint: The first name described what it did: it read the backlinks pointing at a page.
Three words. The middle one is what it spends all day doing.

questions.prompt: Which social network launched under the name Twttr?
questions.hint: The vowels were dropped because five-character usernames were fashionable at the time.
A Japanese company, and the console began life as a CD add-on for a Nintendo machine.
Three words. The first one means you can reach any part of it as quickly as any other.

questions.prompt: Which image format is short for Joint Photographic Experts Group?
questions.hint: Four letters, and it is probably the format of every photo on your phone.

questions.prompt: Which operating system kernel did Linus Torvalds create?
questions.hint: He announced it in 1991 as 'just a hobby, won't be big and professional'.
questions.note: It now runs most of the servers on the internet, and every Android phone.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Amazon's cloud computing platform?
questions.hint: Three words, and it is usually shortened to three letters.

questions.prompt: Which messaging app did Facebook buy for around $19 billion in 2014?
questions.hint: It had 55 staff at the time of the sale.
